excerpt: Fix a full-rank lattice $L\subset\mathbb H$, written as $$ L=\mathbb Z\omega_0+\mathbb Z\omega_1+\mathbb Z\omega_2+\mathbb Z\omega_3, $$ where the four generators are linearly independent over $\mathbb R$. Put $L^*=L\setminus\{0\}$. Use the fixed coordinates $q=t+\sum_{j=1}^3e_jx_j$ and the functions $$ G(q)=\frac{\bar q}{|q|^4},\qquad G_j=\partial_{x_j}G,\quad j=1,2,3. $$ Each bracket in the following lattice sums is a single summand; convergence is asserted for the bracketed sums. :::discussion The naive sum of translates of $G_j$ has borderline decay $|\lambda|^{-4}$ in four dimensions. Subtracting the constant $G_j(\lambda)$ gains an extra power of decay. The individual terms inside a bracket must not be split into divergent lattice sums. ::: ## 2. The elliptic functions ::::construction E-C1 | Regularized first-derivative lattice sums Version: 1 Uses: [lattice setup](#e-d1). Justification: Convergence and regularity in [E1](#e1); periodicity in [E2](#e2). Origin: literature Cite: [[1]](#ref-fueter-1939); [[2, §4, eq. (12), p. 1019]](#ref-krausshar-2001) --- For a full-rank lattice $L\subset\mathbb H$, $j\in\{1,2,3\}$, and $q\in\mathbb H\setminus L$, form the series $$ \wp_{L,j}(q)=G_j(q)+ \sum_{\lambda\in L^*} \bigl[G_j(q+\lambda)-G_j(\lambda)\bigr]. $$ :::: :::discussion Here “elliptic” means lattice-periodic and Fueter-regular away from isolated singularities. E1 and E2 supply these properties for E-C1. ::: ::::proposition E1 | Convergence and regularity Version: 2 Uses: [E-C1](#e-c1), [F1](foundations.md#f1), [F2](foundations.md#f2). Review: pending Formal: none Origin: literature Cite: [[1]](#ref-fueter-1939); [[2, §4, eq. (12), p. 1019]](#ref-krausshar-2001) Proof-cite: [[2, §4, eq. (12), p. 1019]](#ref-krausshar-2001) --- Let $L\subset\mathbb H$ be a full-rank lattice and $j\in\{1,2,3\}$. The series in E-C1 converges absolutely and uniformly on every compact subset of $\mathbb H\setminus L$. It may be differentiated term by term to every real order, with locally uniform convergence of the differentiated series. Its sum is both left and right Fueter-regular. For every $\omega\in L$, the function $$ q\longmapsto\wp_{L,j}(q)-G_j(q-\omega) $$ extends to a smooth, left and right regular function on a neighborhood of $\omega$. :::proof Proof of E1 For a compact set $K\subset\mathbb H\setminus L$, choose $R$ with $|q|\le R$ on $K$. If $|\lambda|>2R$, the segment from $\lambda$ to $\lambda+q$ stays at distance at least $|\lambda|/2$ from $0$. The derivative bound from the foundations page and the mean-value estimate give $$ |G_j(\lambda+q)-G_j(\lambda)| \le C R|\lambda|^{-5}. $$ A full-rank lattice has $O(r^4)$ points in a ball of radius $r$: write $L=A\mathbb Z^4$ for an invertible real matrix $A$ and use equivalence of norms. Summing over dyadic shells now shows $\sum_{\lambda\in L^*}|\lambda|^{-p}<\infty$ for $p>4$. This proves absolute, locally uniform convergence. After $m\ge1$ real derivatives, the constant subtraction vanishes and each tail term is bounded by $C_{K,m}|\lambda|^{-4-m}$. All differentiated series therefore converge locally uniformly. The finitely many terms omitted from these tail estimates are smooth away from their singularities. The standard theorem on locally uniform convergence of derivatives permits differentiation of the sum. Every summand is left and right regular by F1, including the subtracted constant. Termwise differentiation proves regularity of the sum. In a small ball around any lattice point, remove its one singular summand; the remaining series and its derivatives converge uniformly and are regular there. ::: :::: ::::proposition E2 | Parity and periodicity Version: 2 Uses: [E-C1](#e-c1), [E1](#e1), [F2](foundations.md#f2). Review: pending Formal: none Origin: literature Cite: [[1]](#ref-fueter-1939); [[2, §4, eq. (12), p. 1019]](#ref-krausshar-2001) Proof-cite: [[2, §4, eq. (12), p. 1019]](#ref-krausshar-2001) --- Let $L\subset\mathbb H$ be a full-rank lattice and $j\in\{1,2,3\}$. For all $q\in\mathbb H\setminus L$ and $\omega\in L$, $$ \wp_{L,j}(-q)=\wp_{L,j}(q),\qquad \wp_{L,j}(q+\omega)=\wp_{L,j}(q). $$ :::proof Proof of E2 Every first real partial derivative of $\wp_{L,j}$ is the absolutely convergent sum $$ \partial_{x_\mu}\wp_{L,j}(q) =\sum_{\lambda\in L}\partial_{x_\mu}G_j(q+\lambda), \qquad \mu=0,1,2,3,\quad x_0=t. $$ Reindexing this convergent sum shows that the derivatives are $L$-periodic. Hence $$ H_\omega(q)=\wp_{L,j}(q+\omega)-\wp_{L,j}(q) $$ has zero real gradient. The complement of a discrete lattice in $\mathbb R^4$ is path connected, so $H_\omega$ is a constant $c_\omega$. Since $G_j$ is even, reindexing the absolutely convergent defining series by $\lambda\mapsto-\lambda$ shows that $\wp_{L,j}$ is even. Consequently $$ H_\omega(-q-\omega) =\wp_{L,j}(-q)-\wp_{L,j}(-q-\omega) =-H_\omega(q). $$ Both sides are constant in $q$, so $c_\omega=-c_\omega$, and therefore $c_\omega=0$. ::: :::: :::discussion The proof reindexes the absolutely convergent derivative series, then uses evenness to remove the possible constant increment. It does not reindex an unregularized borderline sum. :::

E-C1.statement:
For a full-rank lattice $L\subset\mathbb H$, $j\in\{1,2,3\}$, and $q\in\mathbb H\setminus L$, form the series
$$
\wp_{L,j}(q)=G_j(q)+
\sum_{\lambda\in L^*}
\bigl[G_j(q+\lambda)-G_j(\lambda)\bigr].
$$

E1.statement:
Let $L\subset\mathbb H$ be a full-rank lattice and $j\in\{1,2,3\}$. The series in E-C1 converges absolutely and uniformly on every compact subset of $\mathbb H\setminus L$. It may be differentiated term by term to every real order, with locally uniform convergence of the differentiated series. Its sum is both left and right Fueter-regular.

For every $\omega\in L$, the function
$$
q\longmapsto\wp_{L,j}(q)-G_j(q-\omega)
$$
extends to a smooth, left and right regular function on a neighborhood of $\omega$.

E2.statement:
Let $L\subset\mathbb H$ be a full-rank lattice and $j\in\{1,2,3\}$. For all $q\in\mathbb H\setminus L$ and $\omega\in L$,
$$
\wp_{L,j}(-q)=\wp_{L,j}(q),\qquad
\wp_{L,j}(q+\omega)=\wp_{L,j}(q).
$$
